subject: Data classification & access catalogue — DPA annex questions
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@medsync.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: DPA annex - classification / hybrid deployment diagram request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking our DPA annex. A few items popped up in our review that we need clarified before we circle back to legal for execution:

1) Field-level classification: For PHI/PII fields processed by your inference layer, can you provide a simple CSV mapping that ties model input fields to classification levels (e.g., Sensitive/Restricted/Low) and retention policy per field? We need that to populate our intake.

2) Hybrid deployment dataflow: We run a mixed on-prem + cloud (US/EU) architecture. Please provide a short dataflow diagram that shows where raw tokens, KV cache, and telemetry reside in each deployment topology (hosted, dedicated, private). Specifically: where do logs and aggregated telemetry land, and whether they transit outside the requested region.

3) Subprocessor escrow/activation: We saw references to analytics vendors used for telemetry. For any EU-based subprocessors that could see pseudonymized customer tokens during debugging, what escrow or access gating do you have? Do you support on-demand attestation for a subprocessor's access window?

4) Redaction & logs: Are redaction options available for customer-facing logs (e.g., redacted transcripts for support)? If so, what is the process and lead time?

If you can share the classification CSV and a diagram (a PNG or draw.io export is fine), that would help accelerate our legal review. We have a target to complete DPA review by May 10. Can you confirm if that timeline is feasible?

Best,
Elena Martinez
Sr. Privacy Counsel
MedSync Health

Attachments: MedSync_DPA_annotated.pdf (referenced)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@medsync.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA annex - classification / hybrid deployment diagram request

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (security/infra) and Connor (legal ops) to help close the gaps. Quick responses below and a proposed next step:

1) Field-level classification: we can produce a CSV mapping showing each API field, expected classification, and default retention bucket. I will attach our working matrix (classification_matrix_v1.xlsx) by end of day Monday. Note: we classify prompt tokens as "Transient PII" when they contain user identifiers; derived embeddings are considered "Pseudonymized" per our DPA baseline.

2) Hybrid deployment dataflow: Rishi will provide a diagram for the three deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private) showing where token caching and telemetry are persisted and by whom. Short answer — hosted telemetry lives in our US telemetry cluster by default; Dedicated can be pinned to region and Private deployments are customer-managed (no telemetry retained by Redwood unless explicitly enabled).

3) Subprocessor escrow/activation: We do not have a literal escrow vault for subprocessor access windows, but we maintain time-bound access tokens, just-in-time access approvals, and an access audit log retained for 12 months. For EU subprocessors that may see pseudonymized tokens during debugging, we can provide attestation records and access-session exports on request (standard lead time 3 business days). Rishi, please confirm the lead time and mechanics.

4) Redaction & logs: We support transcript redaction at ingest for hosted customers and a support workflow to produce redacted log exports for investigations. There's a small ops request to enable redaction on legacy ingestion pipelines — lead time ~5 business days.

Next step: we'll attach the CSV and a draw.io export of the dataflow (hybrid_dataflow_v1.drawio.png) by Monday EOD. Connor will circulate a short DPA annex suggestion for the subprocessor gating language. If May 10 is your target, that timeline is tight but doable if we exchange artifacts early next week.

Action items:
- Marissa: attach classification matrix (mon)
- Rishi: produce annotated dataflow and confirm attestation turnaround (mon)
- Connor: draft DPA annex redlines (Tue)

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head, Privacy & Compliance (Product)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (stub) classification_matrix_v1.xlsx

Hi Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from our engineering team so Rishi can target the diagram correctly: 

• For the CSV, can you include an explicit column for "example token shape" (e.g., free-text prompt / json with patient_id) so we can map our ingestion rules?
• Regarding telemetry: will telemetry egress ever route to a third-party analytics sink outside the pinned region for aggregated metrics? If so, which subprocessors operate that sink and where are their data centers located?

On attestation: the legal team will accept a standardized attestation PDF per access window (timestamped, signed, and listing session IDs) — not the raw logs themselves. If you can confirm the attestation export format, we can finalize.

Target: we still want DPA finished May 10; if you can get the CSV + diagram + a draft attestation template to us by Tue EOD (27 Apr), that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Tom Briggs
Legal Operations, MedSync
